title: Transport through an oriented derived tensor product
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $A$ a commutative ring. Work in the unbounded derived category $D=D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ of sheaves of modules on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the specified K-flat derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor] and total tensor convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $T$ be a sheaf of $A_X$-modules, regarded as a complex concentrated in degree zero, and let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Let $\omega\in D$ and fix an isomorphism $\Pi:\omega\xrightarrow{\sim}T[2d]$. Let $\mathcal I$ be a category [def-nagata-category], let $P,H:\mathcal I\to D$ be functors, and suppose given a natural isomorphism $\theta_i:P(i)\otimes_A^L\omega\xrightarrow{\sim}H(i)$.

The canonical second-variable tensor-shift comparison gives a natural isomorphism
$$a_M:(M\otimes_A^LT)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_A^L(T[2d])\qquad(M\in D).$$
On a K-flat representative $Q\to M$, its map in degree $r$ is the identity of $Q^{r+2d}\otimes_A T$. Both differentials are $d_Q\otimes1$; the comparison is the sign-free reindexing, not an unspecified isomorphism of these objects. This formula descends independently of the K-flat representative and is natural in both $M$ and $T$.

The specified morphisms
$$G_i=\theta_i\circ(1_{P(i)}\otimes\Pi^{-1})\circ a_{P(i)}:(P(i)\otimes_A^LT)[2d]\longrightarrow H(i)$$
form a natural isomorphism. Their inverses are exactly
$$a_{P(i)}^{-1}\circ(1_{P(i)}\otimes\Pi)\circ\theta_i^{-1}.$$
In particular the construction uses the given $\Pi$ and $\theta$ with no further scalar or sign choice. No existence or geometric normalization of $\Pi$ or $\theta$ is asserted.

source.place: Three-arrow composite: twist reassociation, inverse orientation and canonical tensor map; extraction of returned proof Steps 1 and 3.

proof.text: Put $n=2d$. For any complexes $E,F$, use the canonical second-variable chain comparison $s^2_n:\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes F[n])\cong\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes F)[n]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. Its coefficient on first-factor degree $p$ is $(-1)^{np}=1$. Hence its inverse is precisely identity reindexing, natural in both chain variables. In particular, for degree-zero $T$ and any complex $Q$, both $(Q\otimes T)[n]^r$ and $(Q\otimes T[n])^r$ are $Q^{r+n}\otimes T$, and both differentials are $d_Q\otimes1$: the shift multiplies the first differential by $(-1)^n=1$ and $d_T=0$. This verifies the stated chain formula, including its direction.

Work on the small skeleton in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] to its constant ring sheaf $A_X$. It supplies the resolving localization equivalence, tensor-model comparisons, and unique extension of natural transformations. The flat-term K-flat resolving class is shift-stable by [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs]; shifting merely reindexes its flat terms. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent] applies to this specified total-tensor bifunctor. Set $a_M=(t^2_n(M,T))^{-1}$. Its statement gives naturality for all derived morphisms in both inputs, not only chain maps. It also identifies $t^2_n$ at a fixed flat-term K-flat first argument with the one-variable comparison on arbitrary second complexes. The latter hypothesis holds because total tensor with a K-flat complex induces a functor on the homotopy category preserving quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs]. The required comparison $e_L$ is constructed, not read off a definition: fix a flat-term K-flat $Q$. Since $Q_hH_Q$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms, it factors uniquely through the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] as $\bar H_Q:D\to D$. The bifunctors $U(M,N)=\bar H_Q(N)$ and $V(M,N)=T(Q_hQ,N)$ are related on $\mathcal P\times\mathcal P$ by the natural isomorphism $c_{Q,B}$, so the extension clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] extends $c$ and $c^{-1}$ uniquely; by uniqueness the extensions are mutually inverse. Since $U,V$ ignore $M$ and $D$ has a zero object, the component does not depend on $M$. Its composite with $Q_h$ is the natural isomorphism $e_{L,B}:Q_hH_Q(B)\cong T(Q_hQ,Q_hB)$, $B\in K(R)$, whose components on $\mathcal P$ are exactly $c_{Q,B}$. With the first resolution $Q$ itself, its source is the object $Q\otimes_AB$ that defines $Q_hQ\otimes_A^LQ_hB$ in [def-weil-derived-tensor]. So $e_L$ is the identification of these specified objects with the values of the descended bifunctor. Consequently, on a flat-term K-flat $Q$ and the unreplaced sheaf $T$, $a$ is exactly the chain map of Step 1. This also identifies the descended bifunctor with the specified K-flat tensor, without a new normalization choice.

proof.text:
For an arbitrary K-flat representative $q:Q\to M$, not assumed termwise flat, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $r:R\to Q$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Then $qr:R\to M$ is another representative. The conditional comparison clause of [lem-weil-derived-tensor-resolution-independent], applied to the actual chain map $r$ and to $T$, respectively $T[n]$, says that $r\otimes1_T$ and $r\otimes1_{T[n]}$ are quasi-isomorphisms and give the canonical model comparisons. Naturality of the chain isomorphism from Step 1 gives
$$ (r\otimes1_{T[n]})\circ a_R^{\rm Ch}=a_Q^{\rm Ch}\circ(r\otimes1_T)[n]. $$
After localization, the two vertical comparisons are invertible. The normalization on $R$ in Step 2 therefore forces the same formula on $Q$. For any two choices $Q,Q'$, their canonical comparisons to the specified derived tensor are exactly those of [lem-weil-derived-tensor-resolution-independent], which obey the cocycle identity. Both chain formulas represent the already constructed $a_M$, so they agree under these comparisons. No direct chain comparison between arbitrary resolutions is assumed, and no flatness of $T$ is used.

proof.text:
Write $F(i)=(P(i)\otimes_A^LT)[n]$, $J(i)=P(i)\otimes_A^LT[n]$ and $B(i)=P(i)\otimes_A^L\omega$. For an arrow $u:i\to j$ let $f=P(u)$. Their arrow maps are $F(u)=(f\otimes1_T)[n]$, $J(u)=f\otimes1_{T[n]}$ and $B(u)=f\otimes1_\omega$, by bifunctoriality of the derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Set $b_i=1_{P(i)}\otimes\Pi^{-1}$. Functoriality gives
$$B(u)\circ b_i=b_j\circ J(u),$$
since both sides are $f\otimes\Pi^{-1}$. Further, $b_i$ is invertible with inverse $1_{P(i)}\otimes\Pi$: their composites are tensor images of the inverse equations for $\Pi$.

Define $G_i=\theta_i\circ b_i\circ a_{P(i)}$, exactly as specified. Naturality in Step 2 and the equation in Step 4, followed by the assumed naturality of $\theta$, give for every $u:i\to j$
$$H(u)\circ G_i=\theta_j\circ B(u)\circ b_i\circ a_{P(i)}=\theta_j\circ b_j\circ J(u)\circ a_{P(i)}=G_j\circ F(u).$$
Thus these actual components form a natural transformation; this calculation uses all arrows of $\mathcal I$ and imposes no finiteness or geometric assumption on that category.

source.place: Three-arrow composite: naturality of the prescribed components

proof.text:
Set $V_i=a_{P(i)}^{-1}\circ(1_{P(i)}\otimes\Pi)\circ\theta_i^{-1}$. Associativity and the inverse equations, in order, give
$$V_iG_i=a_{P(i)}^{-1}(1\otimes\Pi)(1\otimes\Pi^{-1})a_{P(i)}=1_{F(i)},\qquad G_iV_i=\theta_i(1\otimes\Pi^{-1})(1\otimes\Pi)\theta_i^{-1}=1_{H(i)}.$$
Multiplying $H(u)G_i=G_jF(u)$ on the left by $V_j$ and on the right by $V_i$ gives $V_jH(u)=F(u)V_i$, so the displayed inverses are natural too. Hence $G$ is a natural isomorphism with exactly the stated inverse. Every factor was fixed by the hypotheses or by the chain normalization, leaving no scalar or sign choice.
